title: Light-years and space distances
examples: How fast is light actually traveling in space?
If a star is ten light-years away, how far is that?
Does a light-year take a certain amount of time to travel?

explain.say: Today we learn about how far things are in space. We will look at the speed of light first.

items: Light travels at a fixed speed.
This speed does not change in space.
It is very, very fast indeed.

explain.say: The speed of light in a vacuum is about three hundred thousand kilometers every second. This is a constant value.
A light-year is not a measure of time. It is a unit used to measure huge distances in space.
One light-year is the distance light travels in exactly one Earth year. This is a vast distance.
For example, if a star is five light-years away, light took five years to reach us. It is a distance.
In everyday life, we use this idea when talking about distant galaxies. We say they are many light-years away.

faq.q: Is a light-year the same as a year?
faq.a: No, a light-year is a unit of distance, not a unit of time. It tells us how far something is.
asks: Is it a measurement of duration?

faq.q: How fast is light traveling in space?
faq.a: Light always travels at a speed of about three hundred thousand kilometers every second. This speed never changes.
asks: What is the speed of light?

faq.q: If something is ten light-years away, how long did the light take to get here?
faq.a: If it is ten light-years away, the light took exactly ten years to travel that distance to us.
asks: If the distance is 10 ly, what is the time?

faq.q: Can we measure distances using light-years?
faq.a: Yes, astronomers use light-years because the distances in space are so incredibly large. It makes the numbers manageable.
asks: Why not use kilometers for space?

faq.q: Is the speed of light different in space?
faq.a: No, the speed of light remains constant in a vacuum, regardless of where it is in space.

facts: Light travels at approximately three hundred thousand kilometers every second.
A light-year measures the distance light travels in one Earth year.
Light-years are used to measure extremely large distances in space.
The speed of light is constant in a vacuum.

quiz.say: If light travels at three hundred thousand kilometers per second, how far does it travel in one year?

options.show: C: Three hundred thousand kilometers per day.
options.say: C: Three hundred thousand kilometers per day.

options.show: D: Three hundred thousand kilometers per second.
options.say: D: Three hundred thousand kilometers per second.

options.show: A: About nine point four six trillion kilometers.
options.say: A: About nine point four six trillion kilometers.

options.show: B: Three hundred thousand kilometers per minute.
options.say: B: Three hundred thousand kilometers per minute.

quiz.why: The correct answer is A because one year is a long time, and multiplying the constant speed by the number of seconds in a year gives this huge distance.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it only measures the distance for one day, which is too short.
wrong.1: This is wrong because this is the speed, not the total distance covered over an entire year.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it only uses the speed for one minute, not a whole year.

quiz.say: Which unit correctly measures the distance to a nearby star?
quiz.why: Light-years are specifically designed to measure the vast distances between stars and galaxies.

wrong.1: Kilometers are too small a unit for measuring distances across entire star systems.
wrong.2: Seconds measure time, not the physical distance between celestial objects.
wrong.3: Meters are used for very small measurements, not interstellar distances.

quiz.say: If a signal takes twenty years to reach Earth, how far away is the source?

options.show: B: Twenty times the speed of light.
options.say: B: Twenty times the speed of light.

quiz.why: Since the signal traveled at the speed of light, the time taken directly equals the distance in light-years.

wrong.1: This incorrectly multiplies the time by the speed, which gives a unit of distance squared.
wrong.2: This confuses the unit of distance with the unit of time measurement.
wrong.3: This drastically underestimates the distance, ignoring the massive scale of space.
